title: Patch channel policies and fast recovery protocol for LTS and rolling releases
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define unambiguous severity criteria, branch and backport conventions, and an operator-oriented fast recovery protocol for both LTS and rolling channels. This ticket covers: 1) Severity definitions tied to customer-visible SLOs; 2) Branch naming and automated cherry-pick/backport tooling; 3) Rollout gate behavior and emergency rollback mechanics; 4) Runbook updates and PR templates for P0/P1 fixes. Outcome should reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) for regressions affecting inference and management planes and provide deterministic ownership and testing requirements for any patch landing in an LTS channel.

decisions: Severity levels standardized: P0 (service-impacting outage or SLO breach), P1 (degraded customer experience or data loss risk), P2 (non-urgent bug with customer-visible effect), P3 (internal/no-customer-impact).

Patch branch naming: release/<major>.<minor>.patch-<YYYYMMDD>-<short-desc> (example: release/1.18.patch-20251017-evict-kvcache), and LTS backports use release/<major>.<minor>-lts-backport/<cherry-key>.

Backport policy: P0 fixes must be applied to active LTS branches and the rolling main where applicable. P1 fixes evaluated case-by-case; P2/P3 deferred to regular cadence unless customer asks for expedited backport.
Automated cherry-pick pipeline will open candidate backport PRs for each target branch and run an automated presubmit suite; human gate required to merge for LTS branches.

Rollback strategy: prefer revert PR if change is small and idempotent; use emergency configuration flip (feature flag or routing policy) if rollback risks data or infra instability; final option is coordinated node-level rollback using snapshot-based orchestration for stateful components.
Runbook updates required: create 'P0 recovery play' and 'LTS backport checklist' pages with explicit owner assignment and communication templates for customers and status pages.
